questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “What is Rust used for?”?
options: Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
Rust combines high-level abstractions and low-level control with compile-time checks.
Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
questions.answer: Rust combines high-level abstractions and low-level control with compile-time checks.
questions.explanation:
Rust combines high-level abstractions and low-level control with compile-time checks.
Why: Rust is a systems language for software that needs performance, low-level resource control, and strong memory safety. It is used for operating-system components, command-line tools, network services, game infrastructure, WebAssembly, and microcontroller firmware. Ownership and the borrow checker catch many memory errors at compile time, while requiring developers to model ownership, borrowing, and types explicitly.

Company examples: Google uses Rust in the Android platform; AWS's Firecracker virtual-machine monitor and Cloudflare's Pingora proxy are Rust projects. This does not mean all of those companies' software is written in Rust; they choose it for suitable system components. Sources: https://source.android.com/docs/setup/build/rust/building-rust-modules · https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker · https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora
